what_it_does: Treats acne by killing acne-causing bacteria and helping clear blocked pores.
summary_short: Benzoyl peroxide is one of the best-established over-the-counter acne treatments, especially for inflamed pimples. It works quickly for many people but can be drying, irritating, and may bleach towels, clothing, or pillowcases.
summary_long:
Benzoyl peroxide is an acne-fighting ingredient used in cleansers, leave-on gels, creams, and spot treatments. It releases oxygen in the skin, creating an environment that is less friendly to *Cutibacterium acnes*, the bacteria involved in acne. It also has mild pore-clearing and anti-inflammatory effects, which can help reduce red, swollen breakouts.

The evidence for benzoyl peroxide in acne is strong compared with many cosmetic ingredients. It is commonly used for mild to moderate acne and is often recommended because bacteria do not appear to develop resistance to it in the same way they can with topical antibiotics.

Typical over-the-counter strengths are 2.5%, 5%, and 10%. Higher percentages are not always more effective, but they are more likely to sting, peel, or dry out the skin. Many people do well starting with 2.5% or a short-contact cleanser before moving to stronger or leave-on formats.

Irritation is the main downside. Benzoyl peroxide can cause dryness, burning, redness, flaking, and temporary purging-like worsening as clogged pores clear. It can also bleach fabrics and hair, so it is best used carefully around towels, collars, pillowcases, and eyebrows or hairlines.

It pairs well with moisturizers, sunscreen, and acne regimens that include adapalene or topical antibiotics when directed. Use caution when layering with strong exfoliating acids, retinoids, or vitamin C, since the combination can be irritating; some routines separate them by time of day.
